Places let DayCue tell home from the office. They are only stored on this phone.
Add a place so DayCue knows home from the office.
Stop guessing where you are for a while
While paused, DayCue stops using location and activity to decide where you are. Manual choices on Today still work. Place changes are not recorded.
Until I turn it back on
Place and indoor or outdoor are not guessed. Resume to go back to automatic.
If DayCue gets your context wrong

Tap the context line on Today and pick the right place, indoors or outdoors. It holds until you change place, and it never asks you questions. If it is often wrong at one place, make that place’s circle smaller, or mark it Mixed so DayCue stops guessing indoors or outdoors there.
Location while you use the app
DayCue needs your location to add a place from where you stand and to check it. This is the first step.

Without it: no automatic places. DayCue cannot tell home from the office, so reminders tied to a place wait, and “Use my current location” does not work. Manual context, Leaving now and timed reminders still work.
Only approximate location is allowed. A place circle of 50 to 1000 meters needs the precise option.
This is a separate step. With it, Android can tell DayCue when you arrive or leave a place, even when the app is closed. DayCue does not track your route and does not poll your location.

Without it: places are only known while the app is open. Place stays “not sure” in the background, so automatic work sessions never start and the water bottle reminder on leaving a place does not fire. Leaving now still works.
If Android no longer shows the question, turn it on in the app settings.
DayCue gets arrivals and departures from Android, even with the app closed.
What does not work right now
Google Play services are missing or out of date, so places cannot be detected. Manual context still works.
Location is not allowed, so places are not detected and “Use my current location” is unavailable.
Only approximate location is allowed. Places are not detected, and the current-location fix is too coarse for a place circle.

Location is only allowed while the app is open. Places are not detected in the background: place-based reminders wait, work sessions do not start by themselves, and leaving a place does not trigger the bottle reminder.
The phone’s location switch is off. Places are not detected until you turn it on.
Physical activity is not allowed. Away from saved places, walking is not counted as outdoors.
Manual controls on Today, Leaving now and timed reminders work with or without these permissions.
Lets DayCue count a sustained walk away from saved places as outdoors.
Without it: away from saved places DayCue does not guess indoors or outdoors.
A sustained walk away from saved places counts as outdoors.
For example Home, Office or Gym.
A location is saved on this phone.
No location yet. Until you set one, this place is inactive and nothing is detected here.
Location found, but accuracy is about %1$d m and the circle is %2$d m. The circle could miss where you really are. Try again near a window, or use a radius of about %3$d m.
Accuracy is only about %d m, too rough for a place. Nothing was changed. Move near a window and try again, or enter coordinates.
The phone’s location switch is off.
Google Play services are not available, so the current location cannot be read.
Couldn’t get your location. Move near a window and try again, or enter coordinates.
Couldn’t get your location. Try again, or enter coordinates.
Latitude from -90 to 90, longitude from -180 to 180, as decimals. The numbers stay on this phone and are not shown again.
Latitude must be a number from -90 to 90.
Longitude must be a number from -180 to 180.
Map picking is not included. Map tiles come from a map service, and DayCue keeps your places on this phone without contacting one. Use your current location or enter coordinates.
From %1$d to %2$d meters. Smaller is more exact but needs a good fix; larger forgives a rough one.
Indoors when you are here. Sunscreen waits until you go outside.
DayCue won’t guess indoors or outdoors here.
A work session may start or be suggested at this place.
A study session may start or be suggested at this place.
The session starts quietly and you get a “Not working” button to undo it.
One quiet question: Start working? Nothing starts unless you say yes.
Sessions here start only when you start them.
Often arrives a few minutes late. Leaving now is the most reliable.
A routine that is off here is not offered at this place.
You can add the place now and set its location later.
Reminders that used this place stop depending on it. You can undo for a few seconds.
The place and its location are removed from this phone. Habits that used it keep working without it.
It may have been deleted or changed somewhere else.
These are waiting times that stop DayCue from reacting to a short pass-through. Defaults suit most people.
Activity needed before a session starts
Computer activity must continue this long at a work place before a session starts or is suggested.
After this long without computer activity the session pauses and posture timers freeze.
After the computer is locked or asleep this long, the session pauses.
Paused time before the session ends
A session that stays paused this long ends by itself, without a reminder.
Sessions start by themselves only inside these hours.
Off: sessions use your work days from Settings.
A meeting keeps the session going
While a calendar meeting is on, the session does not pause for being away from the computer.
Whether a session starts automatically or is only suggested is set per place, in the place editor.
Time at a place to confirm arrival
You count as arrived after this long inside the circle.
You count as having left after this long outside. Coming back sooner cancels it.
Outdoor signals must hold this long before DayCue says outdoors.
Time to count as indoors again
Short visits inside are ignored. Only a longer one changes outdoors to indoors.
When I’m walking, count as outdoors
Needs the physical activity permission. A sustained walk counts as outdoors, then it goes back to not sure.
Away from saved places, indoors or outdoors stays not sure unless you set it.
Away from saved places counts as outdoors with low confidence. Reminders that need medium confidence will not fire unless you lower their threshold.
DayCue reads your phone’s calendars to remind you before events. It never changes your calendar.
Allow DayCue to read calendars on this phone so it can remind you before meetings and appointments.
Without it: no calendar cues and no meeting awareness. Everything else keeps working.
Read-only access. Titles stay on this phone and are only displayed, never followed or interpreted.
A change in your calendar app reaches DayCue after the phone syncs it: usually within a minute, sometimes up to half an hour. Cues for an event you add right before it starts may be late or missed.
Your last known events are still used. Try again, or check calendar access in app settings.
New calendar cues are paused until it syncs.
Add an account with a calendar in Android settings and turn its sync on.
Calendars whose sync is off on the phone are not listed.
Cue only for events that match a rule below.
Cue before every event in this calendar, using the lead times you set.
Read this calendar for meeting awareness but never cue.
What should DayCue do with events in this calendar?
The first rule that matches an event decides. Drag to reorder.
Add a rule, or use Always cue on a calendar.
See why each event gets a cue or not
Events that already have a reminder
Add a cue when a rule matches
DayCue cues in addition to the reminder already on the event.
Only when the event has no reminder
If the event has its own reminder, DayCue stays quiet about it.
Ignore events that have a reminder
Events with their own reminder never get a DayCue cue.
Cues say the title aloud. Others nearby may hear it.
Cues say something generic like “meeting in 10 minutes”.
Show titles on the lock screen
Off: the lock screen shows a generic cue without the title.
Events that match nothing are left alone.
Every event that matches no rule gets a cue.
Events you answered “maybe” are handled like any other.
Events you answered “maybe” get no cue.
How long a snoozed calendar cue waits.
How many days of events DayCue reads.
Pause calendar cues if not synced for
Old events could be wrong, so DayCue stops calendar cues after this long without a sync.
A rule matches an event when any of its conditions match. Titles are only compared as plain text.
Words separated by commas. Case does not matter.
At least one other person is invited.
The event mentions a known conferencing service.
The event does not block your time.
Matching events never get a cue.
One or more numbers separated by commas, for example 60, 15.
Enter numbers from 0 to 1440, separated by commas.
Used in the sentence “You have a … in 10 minutes”.
While it is on, DayCue knows you are in a meeting and calms cues.
Events that matched it fall back to the next rule or the default.
Enter a name of up to 40 characters.
The next %d days, and what DayCue will do for each event.
No events in the next days
Nothing to cue. Events appear here after the phone syncs.
Event titles come from your calendar. DayCue only displays them as text.
Each kind of cue has its own sound, vibration and spoken phrase. Choose, then press Preview to hear exactly what a real cue does.
When cues collide, the higher one is heard first. The order is fixed.
This cue type was not found
The setup may have changed. Go back and open it again.
When several cues are due together, the higher priority is spoken first and the others wait.
Plays the sound, vibration and phrase locally. Nothing is posted or recorded.
Alarm tones are chosen per alarm in Cues. The ringing alarm always rings its own tone.
The cue says its phrase after the sound.
The phrase for the language in use is spoken. Changes save a moment after you stop typing.
Always speaks English for this cue.
Always speaks Hebrew for this cue.
This cue will use sound only until the voice is installed.
After Android creates a notification channel, Android owns its sound and vibration. If you change them in the system settings, that choice stays, even if you pick another sound here.
Open notification settings for this cue
Use it to change volume behavior, lock screen display or to silence this kind of cue for good.
Reset this cue to its defaults
Spoken cues use the voice installed on your phone. Nothing is sent anywhere.
Off: every cue is sound and vibration only.
Not supported by the speech engine
The %s voice data is not on this phone. Cues in this language use sound only.
To install it: Android Settings, System, Languages, Text-to-speech, the gear next to Google Text-to-speech, then Install voice data and Hebrew. Or press Install voice.
The engine lists no separate voices.
From 0.5 to 2 times. 1.0 is normal. Press Preview on a cue to hear it.
The audio gets quieter for a moment while the cue speaks.
The audio pauses while the cue speaks, then Android lets it continue.
While audio plays, cues only show a notification and nothing is spoken.
Silent notification while a calendar meeting is on.
A short vibration, no sound or speech.
Cues speak during meetings. Others may hear them.
Without headphones or a headset connected, cues do not speak.
These keep a busy moment from turning into a pile of announcements.
Cues due this close together are combined into one.
A cue that arrives sooner than this after another is shown silently.
A merged cue names at most this many items.
A cue that could not be spoken in time is skipped instead of arriving late.
During quiet hours some cues wait and others stay silent.
When Android’s Do Not Disturb is on, cues stay silent as it asks.
Always come through: alarms, medication and a running routine.
Wait until quiet hours end: sunscreen, posture and hydration.
Everything here is optional. DayCue works fully on this phone without any of it.
A small Windows tray app that tells your phone whether the computer is in use. Without it, work sessions are manual, which is a fully supported way to use DayCue.
One signed message about the computer’s state: active, idle, locked or asleep, when it was seen and how long to trust it.
Never sent: keystrokes, mouse movement, screenshots, window titles, app names, browsing, file names or how long you were idle. The signal passes through your relay and no one else.
The companion talks to your phone through your relay. Pair this phone with the relay under Remote access, then come back.
Then in the tray app choose Pair and enter the relay address and this code.
Asking the relay for a code. A relay on a free host can take a minute to wake.
The relay did not answer. This needs a connection. Try again.
Works once, until %s. After that, get a new code.
On the computer: tray icon, right click, Pair, then the relay address and this code.
A signal was ignored: it was not signed by a paired computer
Lets work sessions start and pause from computer activity at your work places.
Not using it is fine. Sessions then start from you, and a calendar meeting counts as activity.
On the computer: tray icon, right click, Unpair. It tells the relay to revoke it and deletes its key.
This phone cannot list or remove computers itself. If a computer is gone, revoke its device on the relay (see the setup guide). Its signals stop counting once they expire.
Check more often at work places
Lets work sessions follow the computer more closely while you are at a work place, inside permitted hours.
Between 3 and 30 minutes. Android may stretch it when the phone is idle.
Battery: each check wakes the phone briefly and makes one network request, only at a work place inside permitted hours. Off by default.
The relay can wake the phone when something changes.
Needs a build with Firebase set up. Until then the phone checks about every 15 minutes or more.
Lets an AI assistant you choose, such as Claude, read and change your setup through a relay you run. You decide what it may do, and the phone has the last word.
Off until you pair this phone with a relay.
This phone was unpaired from the relay
The relay no longer trusts this phone, so nothing is read, changed or sent. Pair again to turn remote access back on.
Paste the pairing link, or enter the relay address and the code from your relay.
Starts with https://. A pasted daycue://pair link fills in the code too.
A relay on a free host can take up to about a minute and a half to wake. Please wait.
Pairing creates a key that never leaves this phone. Your setup is only shared with the relay after pairing, and without medication names or coordinates.
That code isn’t valid or has expired. Get a new one from the relay.
Too many wrong codes. Wait a while, then get a new code.
The relay refused the pairing. Get a new code and try again.
Can’t reach the relay. Pairing needs a connection.
Nothing here has happened yet. Approving needs a press and hold on the review screen.
On. This is the kill switch: turn it off to stop everything at once.
Off. Nothing is pulled, applied or published. Your pairing is kept.
The phone checks the relay when you open the app, after you change something, and about every 15 minutes or more in the background. Android may delay that to save battery.
Ordinary changes apply, sensitive ones ask
Adding things or turning things on happens at once. Sensitive and destructive changes always wait for you.
Every remote change waits for your approval on this phone.
Remote changes are refused. Reading still works for connections that may read.

Ordinary: adding or turning on habits, routines and rules. Sensitive: changing or turning off alarms, quiet hours, speech, context and session rules, moving a place, calendar policy, and anything that deletes.

Off. Medication names never leave this phone, and medication cannot be changed remotely.
On. Names leave the phone to connections that hold this scope, and medication changes are always confirmed here.
Names are chosen by the assistant and are not verified. Revoke any you do not recognize.

An alarm can try to play a Spotify song or playlist. The local tone always rings first, so you are never left without an alarm.

Spotify’s Developer Policy says alarm functionality in an app that uses its SDK needs Spotify’s written approval. This personal app does not have it, so Spotify alarms are your choice and your risk. Spotify may revoke access.
Spotify can only be started from the background in some situations. Do not rely on it to wake you.

A calm personal assistant for recurring habits and routines. Your setup lives on this phone.
DayCue reminds you. It does not give medical advice.
DayCue is built with the following. Tap a font to read its license.
AndroidX, Jetpack Compose, Room, WorkManager, Kotlin and kotlinx
Original sounds made for DayCue, with no third-party audio.
Used for geofences and activity transitions, under Google’s terms for Play services.
What stays here and what can leave
DayCue works on this phone. It has no account, no analytics and no ads.
Your places and their coordinates, calendar titles, medication names and history, your setup and your speech settings. Android’s cloud backup does not include them.
Can leave, only if you set it up

Remote access sends a summary of your setup to the relay you pair with, so an assistant you chose can read it. The desktop companion sends only the computer’s state to that relay. Spotify, if used, runs through the Spotify app.
Coordinates never leave the phone. Medication names leave only if you switch the medication permission on.

Location for places, calendar for cues, physical activity for walking, notifications and alarms for reminders. Each one is optional except notifications, and the app explains what stops working without it.
You can turn remote access off at once, revoke any assistant, export your setup and delete it by clearing the app’s data.
